Single Linear Regression:


Breusch-Pagan Test


Quantile-Quantile (QQ) Plot - Normally Distributed

```{r}

```

Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test - Normally Distributed

```{r}
ks.test(rstandard(mod),"pnorm")
```

Assumptions of homoscedasticity are violated, low p-value. Normally distributed residuals are not violated, high p-value.

Backward Selection

Forward Selection

Spline Regression

Box-Cox Transformation

```{r}
library(MASS)
cleaned_apple_quality$Weight_shifted <- cleaned_apple_quality$Weight + 7
cleaned_apple_quality$Weight <- NULL
mod_max_shifted <- lm(Weight_shifted ~ .*. + I(Size^2) + I(Sweetness^2) + I(Ripeness^2), data = cleaned_apple_quality)
mod_best_shifted <- step(mod_max_shifted,direction="both")
bc <- boxcox(mod_best_shifted)
```

```{r}
bc$x[which.max(bc$y)]
```

$\lambda = 1.07$ is the optimal value for $\lambda$.

```{r}
plot(mod_best_shifted,1)
plot(mod_best_shifted,2)
bptest(mod_best_shifted)
ks.test(rstandard(mod_best_shifted), "pnorm")
```

Remove the influential points, then it should work

Influential Points

WORKED!!!

```{r}
# 1st removal
outlier_1 <- which.max(abs(residuals(mod_best_shifted)))
outlier_1 <- unname(outlier_1)
new_data_1 <- cleaned_apple_quality[-outlier_1, ]
new_model_1 <- lm(Weight_shifted ~ .*. + I(Size^2) + I(Sweetness^2) + I(Ripeness^2),
                  data = new_data_1)

plot(new_model_1, which = 1)
plot(fitted(new_model_1),rstudent(new_model_1))

# 2nd removal
outlier_2 <- which.max(abs(residuals(new_model_1)))
outlier_2 <- unname(outlier_2)
new_data_2 <- new_data_1[-outlier_2, ]
new_model_2 <- lm(Weight_shifted ~ .*. + I(Size^2) + I(Sweetness^2) + I(Ripeness^2),
                  data = new_data_2)

plot(new_model_2, which = 1)
plot(fitted(new_model_2),rstudent(new_model_2))

# 3rd removal
outlier_3 <- which.max(abs(residuals(new_model_2)))
outlier_3 <- unname(outlier_3)
new_data_3 <- new_data_2[-outlier_3, ]
new_model_3 <- lm(Weight_shifted ~ .*. + I(Size^2) + I(Sweetness^2) + I(Ripeness^2),
                  data = new_data_3)

plot(new_model_3, which = 1)
plot(fitted(new_model_3),rstudent(new_model_3))

# 4th removal
outlier_4 <- which.max(abs(residuals(new_model_3)))
outlier_4 <- unname(outlier_4)
new_data_4 <- new_data_3[-outlier_4, ]
new_model_4 <- lm(Weight_shifted ~ .*. + I(Size^2) + I(Sweetness^2) + I(Ripeness^2),
                  data = new_data_4)

plot(new_model_4, which = 1)

# 5th removal
```

Regularization - using new_data_5 since outliers have been removed and Weight_shifted is the predicted y value

```{r}
x_vars <- data.matrix(new_data_5[,c("Size", "Sweetness", "Crunchiness", "Juiciness", "Ripeness", "Acidity", "Quality")])
Y <- new_data_5[, "Weight_shifted"]

library(glmnet)

# alpha = 1 means LASSO regression
mod_0 <- glmnet(x_vars,Y, alpha = 1, lambda = 0)
mod_1 <- glmnet(x_vars,Y, alpha = 1, lambda = 1)
mod_5 <- glmnet(x_vars,Y, alpha = 1, lambda = 5)
mod_10 <- glmnet(x_vars,Y, alpha = 1, lambda = 10)

cv <- cv.glmnet(x_vars, Y, alpha = 1)
plot(cv$glmnet.fit, xvar = "lambda")

 # Ridge Regression
ridge_model <- glmnet(x_vars, Y, alpha = 0)

# LASSO Regression
lasso_model <- glmnet(x_vars, Y, alpha = 1)
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)   # for reproducibility

train_index <- sample(1:nrow(new_data_5), size = 0.75 * nrow(new_data_5)) 

train_data <- new_data_5[train_index, ]
test_data  <- new_data_5[-train_index, ]
train_data$Type <- "Train"
test_data$Type <- "Test"

mod <- lm(Weight_shifted ~ .,new_data_5)
x_train <- data.matrix(train_data[, c("Size","Sweetness","Crunchiness",
                                      "Juiciness","Ripeness","Acidity","Quality")])
y_train <- train_data$Weight_shifted
x_test <- data.matrix(test_data[, c("Size","Sweetness","Crunchiness",
                                    "Juiciness","Ripeness","Acidity","Quality")])
y_test <- test_data$Weight_shifted

# Note, y_pred is the predictions of the out-of-sample data points from our in sample predictions
mean(resid(mod))
var(resid(mod))
#mean(y_pred)
#var(y_pred) 


library(glmnet)

X <- model.matrix(Weight_shifted ~ ., new_data_5)
y <- new_data_5$Weight_shifted

# LASSO
lam_lasso <- cv.glmnet(x=X, y=y,nfolds=5,alpha=1)
# alpha = 1 means we are doing LASSO
plot(lam_lasso) # Plots the estimates of the lambda parameters plus a 95% confidence intervals
lam_lasso
# min is the value of lambda that minimizes the MSPE and 1se adds a standard error to it
lambda_lasso <- lam_lasso$lambda.min

# Ridge
lam_ridge <- cv.glmnet(x=X,y=y,nfolds=5,alpha=0)
plot(lam_ridge)
lam_ridge
lambda_ridge <- lam_ridge$lambda.min

# Let's see which one produces the smallest MSPE
lam_lasso$cvm[lam_lasso$lambda == lambda_lasso] # extracting the mspe for the optimal lambda answer: 1.804167

# Let's see it for ridge = 1.82235
lambda_ridge <- lam_ridge$lambda.min
lam_ridge$cvm[lam_ridge$lambda == lambda_ridge]
```

Elastic

```{r}
K <- 5 # 5 fold cross validation
foldid <- sample(rep(1:K, length.out = nrow(new_data_5)))
lam_lasso <- cv.glmnet(x=X, y=y,foldid=foldid,alpha=1)
lambda_lasso <- lam_lasso$lambda.min
lam_lasso$cvm[lam_lasso$lambda == lambda_lasso]

lam_ridge <- cv.glmnet(x=X, y=y,foldid=foldid,alpha=0)
lambda_ridge <- lam_ridge$lambda.min
lam_ridge$cvm[lam_ridge$lambda == lambda_ridge]

# Now, let's do some cross-validation for elastic net
alpha <- seq(0,1,0.05)
alpha_cv <- NULL
for (a in alpha){
  lam_a <- cv.glmnet(x=X, y=y, foldid=foldid, alpha=a)
  lambda <- lam_a$lambda.min
  alpha_cv <- c(alpha_cv, lam_a$cvm[lam_a$lambda == lambda])
}
plot(alpha, alpha_cv)
a <- alpha[which.min(alpha_cv)]
```

Calculate the prediction lines

```{r}
ex <- glmnet(x=X, y=y,alpha=1)
pred_ex <- predict(ex,newx=as.matrix(new_data_5), s=0.05) # newx is the matrix of explanatory variables in your model, and s is the smoothing parameter 
# You have to specify a newx
# You can also extract the coefficients from a cv.glmnet
# Let's extract the predictions from our optimal LASSO and ridge
pred_lasso <- predict(lam_lasso, newx=as.matrix(new_data_5), s="lambda.min")
pred_ridge <- predict(lam_ridge, newx=as.matrix(new_data_5), s="lambda.min")
# You can aslo use an elastic net but must specify your alpha beforehand
ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(x=1:1064, y=y), color = "black", alpha = 0.25, size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(aes(x=1:1064, y=pred_lasso), colour="green", alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(x=1:1064, y=pred_ridge), colour="brown", alpha = 0.6, size = 2)
```

Can't really see the different colors since the predicted values (pred_lasso and pred_ridge) are extremely close to each other and close to y. Thus the points lie almost exactly on top of each other.

Lasso coefficients - significant variables and actionable insights

```{r}
coef(lam_lasso, s = lambda_lasso)
```
